correctness.rationale: The signature identity S(uv)=S(u)S(v) and its coefficients are exact. The base pairs give q-1 independent degree-one directions at fixed length and L_q(2) elementary free Lie commutators. The identity Δ(1+X_a)B-B(1+X_a)Δ shows the inductive leading term [P,X_a+C], with all lower degrees zero; det(I+c1^T)=1+|U|>0 and [L_j,L_1]=L_(j+1) guarantee spanning and permit exact basis selection. Equal pair lengths are invariant. Uniform expansion acts by X_a -> (1+X_a)^m-1 and scales degree-j leading differences by m^j. The telescoped digit-block differences and basis independence prove injectivity by the least differing homogeneous level, with genuine base-2^j uniqueness. All words have equal length C(2^R-1), and the nested occurrence identity proves distinction of actual k-decks, not merely shorter signatures. Common suffix padding is cancellable in the truncated algebra. The maximal R relation yields an Ω(n^E) bound at every large n. Theorem 5.1 of the cited source supplies the upper bound; k=1 follows from exact compositions. A dependency-free checker independently confirmed exact finite ranks, scaling, and three full length-k-deck codebooks; no finite check is used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The all-fixed-q,k lower bound is explicitly open as Conjecture 8.1 in the closely matching September 2026 primary work; its Theorem 5.1 is an upper bound and its lower constructions cover only k<=2 or binary k=3. The positive-word commutator spanning recursion and base-2^j injection are not entailed by those special cases. The older full-text binomial-equivalence treatment establishes an upper bound and k=2 growth only. Comparisons with closely related published mathematical statements revealed no implication covering the all-parameter theorem. Residual risk remains from unindexed work and an access-restricted earlier full text.

value.rationale: Theorem settles the explicitly stated Conjecture 8.1 of a 2026 primary research paper for every fixed alphabet and read length, closing the gap between its general polynomial upper bound and known lower bounds restricted to k<=2 or binary k=3. It gives a constructive explanation of why every weighted Lyndon degree is realizable at the full asymptotic exponent; the distinction matters for exact zero-error capacity growth of subsequence-readout channels. Neither proof correctness nor numerical experimentation alone is used as value evidence.
